[Section] Comparing BV2009 with the Oracle Method
[source_id=17] We denote the stopping method published in BIBREF4 as BV2009. This stopping method will stop the active learning process if the mean of the three previous kappa agreement values between consecutive models is above a threshold. For larger batch percents, note that BV2009 stops later than the optimal Oracle Method point.
[source_id=18] We ran BV2009 with smaller window sizes for each of our different batch sizes. Our results are summarized for a window size of one in the row ``BV2009 (Window Size = 1)'' in Table~ SECREF4 . When using a window size of one, BV2009 is able to stop with a smaller number of annotations than when using a window size of three. This is done without losing much F-Measure. The next subsection provides an explanation as to why smaller window sizes are more effective than larger window sizes when larger batch sizes are used.
